When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

`textstats` counts words and lines in a piece of text, for a command-line
report the docs team runs on draft chapters.

### Strengths
- **The deviation from the plan is correct and was needed.** The plan's `text.split(" ")` breaks design.md req 1 three ways: `""` gives 1 instead of 0, runs of spaces are counted more than once, and tabs and newlines don't separate words. It would also have failed the plan's own Task 2 test, because `"one two\nthree four"` gives 3 words. `textstats/count.py:5` uses `len(text.split())`, which matches req 1 exactly. The pre-flight scan in the ledger caught and documented this.
- **`tests/test_count.py:10-26` covers every clause of req 1.** There are tests for tabs, newlines, a run of mixed whitespace counting once, leading and trailing whitespace, empty text and whitespace-only text. Each one would fail under the plan's `split(" ")`, so they test real behaviour.
- **`textstats/report.py:4-5` matches req 2 exactly** and reuses `count_words` without duplicating it.
- **Stdlib only.** `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` runs 8 tests and all pass. I re-ran them.
- The module docstring the user asked for is present (`textstats/count.py:1`). It's one line and changes no behaviour.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

#### Important (Should Fix)
None.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)
1. **The commit message of 65b5ec2 is malformed.** There is no blank line between `feat: report` and `Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. I checked it:
   - `git log -1 --format=%s 65b5ec2` gives `feat: report Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
   - `%(trailers:only)` gives nothing, so git doesn't see the attribution as a trailer.
   - For comparison, bbd7b48 and f46dec1 are formatted correctly.

   Why it matters: once merged, the bad subject is permanent in `main`, and tools that read trailers won't find the co-author. The code is unaffected. The model named (Haiku) matches the Task 2 implementer in the ledger, so only the formatting is wrong. Fix: reword the tip commit so the subject is `feat: report`, followed by a blank line and then the trailer. It's the tip commit, so this is cheap before merge.
2. **`tests/test_report.py:7-8` has only the happy-path test.** I checked `report` by hand and it already behaves correctly:

   | Input | Result |
   |---|---|
   | `""` | `{'words': 0, 'lines': 0}` |
   | `"a\n"` | lines 1 |
   | `"a\n\nb"` | lines 3 |
   | `"\n"` | `{'words': 0, 'lines': 1}` |

   The gap is in the tests, not the code. Adding a test for `""` and one for a trailing newline would pin the `splitlines` behaviour that req 2 names.
3. **There is no `.gitignore`, so `tests/__pycache__/` and `textstats/__pycache__/` show up as untracked.** This isn't in the spec or plan, and nothing was committed by mistake. Adding a `.gitignore` with `__pycache__/` would tidy it.

### Deferred-minor triage
| Ledger item | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Task 1: no .gitignore, `__pycache__` untracked | **Not required for merge.** Housekeeping only, not in the spec, and nothing bad was committed. Optional follow-up. |
| Task 2: report has only the happy-path test | **Not required for merge.** The behaviour is correct (verified above), so this is a test-coverage nicety. A good small follow-up. |
| Task 2: Co-Authored-By trailer jammed into subject of 65b5ec2 | **Fix before merge.** It isn't a code defect, but it is the only item that becomes permanent and messier to fix after merge. Today it's a one-commit reword at the branch tip. |

Note: the per-task Codex gates didn't run because Codex isn't installed, so this review is the only check beyond the per-task reviewers. I found nothing that the missing gate would have needed to catch.

### Recommendations
- Reword 65b5ec2 before merging.
- Optionally add the two `report` edge-case tests and a `.gitignore` in a follow-up commit.
- The plan has a problem of its own: Task 1 step 3 contradicted the binding spec and conflicted with Task 2. If plan.md will be reused, update it to `split()` so it agrees with design.md.

### Assessment
**Ready to merge?** With fixes

**Reasoning:** The code meets every requirement in design.md, the one deviation from the plan was needed and is well tested, and all tests pass. The only thing to do before merge is reword the 65b5ec2 commit message, which would otherwise land in `main` permanently.
